newsitem.title: USA: Amtrak places $46 million order for GM locomotives.
newsitem.headline: Amtrak places $46 million order for GM locomotives.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Wednesday that Amtrak placed a $46 million order for 21 F59PHI locomotives for use in the national passenger railroad's West Coast operations.

Richard Fleming, a spokesman for GM's Electro-Motive Division in La Grange, Ill., said the deal represents the first time that Amtrak has ordered the locomotives. GM's previous customers for the aerodynamic, fuel-efficient locomotives have been regional commuter rail systems.
Amtrak said the new locomotives, to be delivered in March 1998 through August 1998, will operate on the San Diegans, Capitols, San Joaquins, Capitols and Pacific North West Corridor routes.
They will retire older GM F40 diesel locomotives, some of which are 20 years old.
